title: Contextual column compression and dynamic density thermostat for deep virtualized tables
creator: Anika Rao
description: Problem: Large result sets used by customers (logs, audit trails, user lists) are hard to scan on narrow screens. Existing density modes and column pinning are helpful but noisy when there are many low-priority columns. Goal: introduce a contextual column compression mode plus a dynamic density thermostat that automatically adjusts per-row density based on visual relevance signals and user intent. This should reduce horizontal scroll, preserve primary column legibility, and play nicely with keyboard navigation, screen readers, and virtualization measured rendering. Scope: - UI exploration of compressed column states (ellipsis, stacked micro-rows, inline summary chips) - Thermostat control: manual slider + "smart" auto mode that adapts to available width and user actions - Interaction for temporarily expanding a compressed column (hover/keyboard focus/tap) - Integration with existing column-resize, sort, filter affordances, and column visibility settings - Performance budget to avoid adding expensive DOM measurement loops Constraints: must work with our existing virtualized renderer (continuous virtualization), avoid layout thrashing, be compatible with server-side persisted user column preferences, and not require model changes to existing APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Design specs cover: collapsed column visual treatment, expanded preview state, keyboard accessible expand/collapse, and mobile fallback
Prototype demonstrates the thermostat auto mode responding to container width changes and manual override toggles
Engineering notes list measurable performance budget and how to avoid full reflows (use CSS transforms, clip-paths, and virtualized placeholder widths)
A11y checklist completed: focus order preserved, aria-expanded/aria-controls applied, screen reader text for compressed content summaries
Integration checklist with Console routing: no regressions in sort/filter interactions or persisted user layouts
design_decisions: Prefer progressive visual compression (truncate -> compact chip -> stacked micro-row) over abrupt hiding to retain information scent
Expose a single thermostat control in the column menu and a global setting in Table prefs for users who want predictable behavior
Use CSS-only transitions where possible; reserve JS for measuring breakpoints and toggling CSS classes to minimize repaint cost
Temporary expansion will be based on pointer hover or keyboard focus; expansion does not mutate layout outside the row to avoid shifting neighboring rows
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces horizontal scrolling and surface area for quick scanning; works with virtualization without rendering hidden columns fully
Cons: compressed representations lose some inline context (e.g., long status messages require a click to view full text); increased cognitive load for new users vs explicit column hide
Performance tradeoff: measuring column importance requires heuristics (column priority, recent interactions) which may produce imperfect results initially
